tagline: The Inca capital sits at 3,400 metres, its Spanish churches built on earthquake-proof Inca walls — and the gateway to Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley.
overview: Cusco was the navel of the Inca Empire — its name means 'centre' in Quechua. When the Spanish conquered it in 1533 they built their churches and palaces directly on Inca foundations, so today colonial arcades rise over walls of perfectly fitted stone.

The city itself is a wonder: the Plaza de Armas ringed by arcades, the cathedral holding the famous painting of a Last Supper with guinea pig, and the Qorikancha, once the Incas' richest temple of the sun. Above town, the zigzag walls of Sacsayhuamán fit stones weighing over 100 tonnes.

Almost everyone is passing through — to Machu Picchu by train or the Inca Trail, to the Sacred Valley's markets and ruins, to Rainbow Mountain's striped slopes or Humantay's turquoise lake. At 3,400 metres, take the first day easy and drink the coca tea.

funFacts.title: THE INCAS' CAPITAL
funFacts.text: Cusco was the capital of Tawantinsuyu, the largest empire in pre-Columbian America.

funFacts.title: EARTHQUAKE-PROOF STONES
funFacts.text: Inca walls fitted without mortar have survived earthquakes that toppled the Spanish buildings on top.

funFacts.title: A TEMPLE UNDER A CHURCH
funFacts.text: The Convent of Santo Domingo stands on Qorikancha, the Incas' gold-covered Temple of the Sun.

funFacts.title: GUINEA PIG FOR SUPPER
funFacts.text: The cathedral holds a famous painting of the Last Supper where Jesus and the disciples eat cuy — guinea pig.

funFacts.title: A CITY SHAPED LIKE A PUMA
funFacts.text: The Incas supposedly laid out Cusco in the shape of a puma, with Sacsayhuamán as the head.

funFacts.title: HIGHER THAN THE CITY
funFacts.text: At 3,400 metres, Cusco is higher than most of the Inca sites visitors use it to reach.

funFacts.title: THE INCA TRAIL
funFacts.text: The 4-day trail to Machu Picchu is so popular that permits sell out months ahead.

funFacts.title: A RAINBOW MOUNTAIN
funFacts.text: Vinicunca's stripes of mineral colour became world-famous after snow melt revealed them around 2015.

funFacts.title: STONE OF TWELVE ANGLES
funFacts.text: A famous street stone fits into its wall with twelve angles, without mortar.

funFacts.title: WORLD HERITAGE TWICE
funFacts.text: The historic centre is UNESCO-listed, and the surrounding valley holds dozens of Inca sites.
